kind: MEASURED: plain EXPLAIN on production (the statements were planned, never executed). Read-only session, 8 s statement timeout, no planner setting changed.
question: Can the EXISTING raw-text trigram indexes serve the independently defined semantics?
accessPathTested: Per required word of 3+ characters: raw_column ~* 'O[apostrophes]*N[apostrophes]*E[apostrophes]*I[apostrophes]*L' -- the only raw-text condition the semantics imply, because a removed apostrophe may sit between any two letters of the raw value. Words under 3 characters have no condition at all.

plans.name: ONeil Plumbing
plans.licenses: Bitmap Index Scan on both license trigram indexes with total cost 96,120 + 76,899 -- the cost of reading each index in full: pg_trgm extracts no selective trigram from a pattern with an optional character between every letter

plans.name: R & T
plans.licenses: Seq Scan on licenses (1,268,855 rows): initials have no trigram

forComparison: The review-1 plan that used raw ILIKE fragments cost ~2,100 index candidates, but its semantics were the ones review 2 rejected (apostrophe threshold, raw-fragment gate).
conclusion: Alternative A fails. No condition on raw text is both implied by the semantics and selective: apostrophes can fall anywhere, initials have no trigram, and one-word common names stay cache-bound. These statements were deliberately NOT executed on production: each is a sequential scan of a 0.26 GB / 1.33 GB table.

productionFacts.locale: en_US.UTF-8 (upper('josé müller') = 'JOSÉ MÜLLER': non-ASCII case folding works)
productionFacts.observation: The five name trigram indexes total 368 MB, more than shared_buffers (256 MB). They cannot all stay resident, which matches the cold 14.8-18.9 s vs warm 0.23 s swing measured in review 1.
